day1_insight: Recent rain (16 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: 16 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; and high tide level is lowering risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls. The most recent sample, 6 days ago, was excellent at 10 MPN/100mL.
day3_insight: There's been no rain at all lately, so stormwater runoff isn't a factor right now. The model's main signals right now: high tide level is lowering risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; high tide timing is lowering risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; and no rain has fallen, so nothing is washing off the land into the surf. The most recent sample, 5 days ago, was excellent at 5 MPN/100mL.
